findings.reason: a node implementing §8 must choose between breaking a cited test and inventing the tail's carrier and its rendering, and either reading is a different deliverable from the one the section declares.
findings.text: §8 says the settle row "gains a tail" while "That text stays as it is, because tests/test_a_pane_settles_when_no_work_is_live.py and tests/test_a_pane_does_not_settle_during_admission.py assert it", but the cited test asserts `settles[0]["line"] == f"no live work in {SESSION} since {stamp}"` (tests/test_a_pane_does_not_settle_during_admission.py:340), an exact equality on the row's only text field, so appending the tail to `line` fails the very test the section cites as its reason for not touching the text, while putting it anywhere else leaves the done-when's "exactly one drain line naming one run that needs the coordinator" with no named carrier and no named renderer

findings.reason: without a control that withholds the new tail and shows a case go red, the node cannot show that the tail, rather than the pre-existing settle row it extends, is what its assertion measured.
findings.text: §8's done-when runs three cases (one drain line naming the run, a peer session's live run not preventing it, a second drain line after promotion) but declares no negative control, where §7 and §10 each name one and execute it

findings.reason: the guard against the list becoming a dispatch fence cannot fail as written, so the section reports a protection it does not hold; a positive control that greps the new module for its own symbol and requires a hit would make the absence mean something.
findings.text: §10's done-when records "No dispatch path consults the list, asserted by the test grepping `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` for the new function's name", which is an absence with nothing behind it: at the node's base `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` names neither the new module nor its function, and §10's write paths do not include that file, so the grep prints the same empty result whether the change is made or not

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves at head: `_needs_you_runs` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:924), `_follow_watch_lines` (:1767), `_tick` (:2106), `_follower_settle_line` (:1116), `FLEET_BLOCKED_STATES` and `FLEET_UNPROMOTED_STATES` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1370, :1378), `overdue_unreconciled_runs` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:292), `_follower_liveness` and `_unattended_seconds` (reckon/crew/runs.py), the `crew view` read surface and `reckon/mcp_views.py`'s `VIEW_NAMES`, and each named test file exists.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — §8's done-when names no negative control at all, and §10's "no dispatch path consults…" grep guard is an assertion that cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the three units write their tests into the repository and their gates and negative controls under the run directory, not into a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new modules are named by capability (`reckon/crew/needs_you.py`, `reckon/crew/forgotten_runs.py`, the drain line, the needs-you line); no phase, sprint, ticket or version label reaches a symbol, a filename or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's mechanism does not reach its own done-when: the section says the settle row "gains a tail" while "That text stays as it is", and the test it cites for keeping the text asserts the row's `line` equals the settle text exactly, so the tail has no carrier the mechanism names. The other two reasoning checks pass: the root cause §7 states matches its evidence, and each unit names the production caller it runs through.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 closes the needs-you line, §8 closes the drain-line tail, §10 closes the forgotten-run report; each names one deliverable with one done-when.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the only sections declared `implementable` are §7, §8 and §10; `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s8: [the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches#s7]`, which matches §8's own "It builds after §7, which creates the module", and all three are carried by the open followup `f-tmstwiw-007-012` ("Build the open monitor sections (§7–§12)"), so no implementable node is left without a carrier and no declared edge points at the wrong node.
